claims.claim: Arena can be used as a command-line tool or as a Go library
promptarena is the CLI binary name
promptarena run is a subcommand that runs a config
The -c flag on promptarena run takes an arena config file path
The CLI is configured with YAML configuration files
engine.NewEngine takes five arguments: cfg, providerReg, promptReg, mcpReg, executor
eng.ExecuteRuns(ctx, plan, 4) returns two values: runIDs and an error
ExecuteRuns takes a context, a plan, and a concurrency integer (4 in example)
The programmatic approach means importing Arena as a Go library and controlling it from code
promptarena run accepts a --scenario flag
promptarena run accepts a --provider flag
claude is a provider name the --provider flag accepts
promptarena run accepts a --verbose flag
The CLI needs no compilation step to run a test (prebuilt binary, YAML config)
promptarena run accepts a --ci flag
promptarena run accepts a --format flag with junit as a value
The arena config has a top-level scenarios list
Each scenarios entry takes a file key that points to a scenario YAML
Running promptarena run with no subcommand flags starts an interactive TUI
The TUI shows progress, logs and results while tests run
Built-in CLI outputs are JSON, HTML, JUnit and Markdown
Calling promptarena run from another program via a shell call (system) requires parsing its output
The engine package can be imported from application code to embed a test run
buildTestConfig(prompt) is a function that builds a config from a prompt (illustrative helper)
setupEngine(cfg) returns an engine (illustrative helper)
runTests(eng) returns results from an engine (illustrative helper)
validateResults(results) returns an error (illustrative helper)
config.Scenario is a type in a package named config
A map of string to *config.Scenario is used to hold scenarios
cfg.LoadedScenarios is a field on the config that takes a map of scenarios
loadFromDB() returns a collection of conversations (illustrative helper)
buildScenario(conversation) returns a *config.Scenario (illustrative helper)
adjustConfig(cfg, results) and allPassed(results) are used to rerun a test with an adjusted config (illustrative helpers)
Run results are returned as result objects that can be iterated directly
extractMetrics(result), sendToDatadog(metrics), updateDashboard(metrics) are helper functions (illustrative)
engine.Engine is an exported type in the engine package
TestRunner methods RunWithRetry, CompareProviders, GenerateReport are user-defined (illustrative)
Each programmatic change requires editing Go code, recompiling, then running
promptarena run -c regression-tests.yaml --ci is a valid CLI invocation
custom-tests/main.go is a Go program run with go run in the hybrid pattern (illustrative path)
exec.Command('promptarena', 'run', 'generated.arena.yaml') runs the CLI on a generated config
buildConfigFromData() and saveToYAML(cfg, path) produce a YAML arena config (illustrative helpers)
./custom-test-runner is a binary built from Go code (illustrative)
engine.NewEngineFromConfigFile(path) loads an existing arena YAML config and returns an engine
Existing YAML arena configs can be reused unchanged by the programmatic API
executeAndProcess(eng) runs the engine and processes results (illustrative helper)
buildConfig() constructs an arena config in Go code (illustrative helper)
CLI startup time is about 100-500ms (Go binary startup)
CLI overhead is minimal (one process per run)
CLI memory is isolated per execution (separate process)
Programmatic startup time is 0ms because the engine runs in the same process
Programmatic overhead is none (native function calls)
Programmatic memory is shared with the host application
promptarena run accepts a --verbose flag for debugging (repeat of flag claim, debugging section)
promptarena debug is a subcommand that accepts a --config flag
promptarena config-inspect is a subcommand
err := eng.ExecuteRuns(ctx, plan, 4) assigns a single return value (error) from ExecuteRuns
promptarena run -c product-tests.yaml --ci is a valid CLI invocation (example)
buildConfigForCustomer(customer) and notifyCustomer(customer, results) are illustrative helpers
runTests(cfg) accepts a config, while line 122 uses runTests(eng) on an engine (signature inconsistency in examples)
promptarena run -c benchmarks/suite.arena.yaml is a valid CLI invocation (example)
experiments/ablation-study.go is a Go file run with go run (illustrative path)
